entries.question: What are the rewards and reversibility at 2 and 4 Faction Influence, and does tying the Alliance holder at 4 steal the Alliance?

observed_response.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; that VP is lost below 2 and regained on returning to 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first player to 4 also gets the Alliance and 1 VP, which stays tied to holding that token. Merely tying the holder at 4 does not take it; an opponent must rise higher (subject to the stated FAQ holder-loss rules).
observed_response.evidence: Scoring: 2 Influence VP reverses below 2; 4 Influence has separate track bonus retained below 4 and Alliance +1 VP; ‘Tying the current holder does not steal the Alliance: an opponent must rise higher.’

key_entry.expected_answer: Reach 2 gets 1 VP lost below 2. Reach 4 gets track bonus retained if falling below, can earn again on re-reaching. First to 4 gets Alliance and its VP; tie does not steal, opponent must rise higher. Transfer loses old holder VP and gives new holder VP.

material_parts.reason: Explicitly gives +1 VP at 2, loss below 2, and recovery on returning.
Explicitly distinguishes the retained printed bonus and repeat earning on returning to 4.

material_parts.part: Alliance acquisition, tie, and both transfer score effects
material_parts.reason: The first player receives the Alliance and 1 VP; the statement that this VP stays tied to holding that token means its former holder ceases to have that VP and its new holder has it. Together with the explicit higher-than-holder transfer threshold and no transfer on a tie, this conveys both score consequences without needing the literal verbs lose/gain.

entries.reason: Complete semantic answer. “That VP ... stays tied to holding that token” refers to the stated single Alliance VP, and is sufficient to express reversibility and score following a transfer. The reference to additional FAQ holder-loss rules does not leave the asked threshold/tie/transfer rule unresolved. No material contradiction.

entries.question: Can you Infiltrate your own occupied board space, use a Spy without playing a card, or recall two connected Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement?

observed_response.answer: Infiltrate is described for sending to a board space occupied by another player; using it to bypass your own occupied space is unsupported. A Spy cannot send an Agent without playing a card for the Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you may use one for Infiltrate and another for Gather Intelligence.
observed_response.evidence: Special Rules defines Infiltrate only for another player’s Agent; FAQ says recalling Spy ‘still requires playing a card for the Agent turn’ and permits one Infiltrate plus one Gather, ‘never two to Gather Intelligence.’ Own-occupancy case not stated.

key_entry.expected_answer: No to all. Infiltrate bypasses another player Agent; still play a card and meet entry costs/requirements. Two Spies can pay different effects (Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence), not duplicate Gather Intelligence.
key_entry.novelty: Spy ownership and per-effect recall limits

material_parts.reason: Calls the use unsupported, and same-question evidence expressly says the own-occupancy case is not stated. This is abstention about the summary, not a definite ruling that the move is illegal.

material_parts.part: Spy without playing an Agent-turn card
material_parts.reason: Explicitly states a Spy cannot send an Agent without playing a card.

material_parts.part: Two Gather Intelligence recalls on one placement
material_parts.reason: Explicitly prohibits two Gather Intelligence recalls and allows one of each different effect.

entries.reason: The first of the three requested yes/no rules is left unresolved. Accurate descriptions of another-player Infiltrate and the other two prohibitions do not substitute for deciding the own-space question. The missing explicit entry-cost reminder is explanatory background rather than a separate asked scenario. No material contradiction.

entries.question: For a two-player Rival, what do House Hagal Maker Hooks and Shield Wall removal icons do if it already has Hooks, lacks Hooks, or the wall is already gone?

observed_response.answer: A Hagal Maker Hooks icon takes a token only if the Rival needs one; if it already has Hooks it does nothing. A Shield Wall removal effect works only if the Rival has Maker Hooks; without them it is ignored. If the Wall is already gone, there is no token to remove; further behavior is not stated.
observed_response.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: Hooks icon takes token if needed; Shield Wall effect removes wall only if Rival has Hooks, otherwise ignore. Already-removed case not stated explicitly.

key_entry.expected_answer: Maker Hooks icon takes a token onto garrison only if Rival lacks one. Shield Wall removal effect removes the wall if Rival has Hooks and wall remains; without Hooks ignore the removal effect, and if wall already gone no wall remains to remove.
key_entry.source_references: Supplements PDF p4 Hagal icon explanations
key_entry.novelty: Rival-only prerequisite on wall removal, and idempotent Hooks acquisition

material_parts.part: Hooks icon when lacking/already holding Hooks
material_parts.reason: Takes a token only if needed, and explicitly does nothing if already held.
Requires Hooks and otherwise is ignored.
Explicitly says there is no token to remove. This resolves the requested Wall-removal outcome and matches the key’s formulation that no wall remains to remove.

entries.reason: All requested conditional outcomes are stated. The caveats “further behavior is not stated” and “not stated explicitly” do not retract the explicit no-token-to-remove outcome. The question does not request a catalogue of hypothetical further behavior, and the key itself resolves this case as no Wall remaining to remove. It would over-require the answer to demand the literal phrase no further effect once the requested removal is already resolved. The token’s garrison location is unasked background, not a missing icon-outcome rule.

entries.question: Before the first round without CHOAM, how are each human starter deck, Intrigue deck, Imperium deck/Row and Reserve stacks prepared? Where do the human Combat marker, three Spies, Councilor and Control markers start?

observed_response.answer: Each human shuffles the listed 10-card starting deck and places it face down. Shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks; deal five Imperium cards face up as the Row; set out Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow Reserve stacks. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked cards. Each human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor and Control markers are placed in supply, with Control markers and Councilor in view. The specific initial board placement of all three Spies/Councilor/control markers beyond supply/in-view is unsupported.
observed_response.evidence: Setup gives deck composition/shuffle and Imperium row/reserves/CHOAM omission; Combat marker at 0; ‘remaining components (including your 3 Spies) in your supply, in clear view’; exact individual component placements not otherwise given.

key_entry.expected_answer: Each human shuffles their identical ten-card starting deck and puts it face down in their supply left of their Leader. Omit CHOAM-marked Imperium/Intrigue cards, shuffle the Intrigue and Imperium decks face down, deal five Imperium cards face up, and place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks next to the Row. Human Combat marker starts at zero on the indicated initial side; three Spies, Councilor and Control markers start in their supply in clear view.
